title: Why Leaves Change Color: Falling Leaves

scenes.title: THE LEAF LETS GO
scenes.caption: A separation layer forms at the stem.
scenes.narration: As the leaf ages, a layer of cells forms where the leaf joins the twig. This weakens the connection in a controlled way.

scenes.title: AUTUMN ON THE GROUND
scenes.caption: Leaves fall and cover the forest floor.
scenes.narration: Once the connection is ready, wind or gravity can carry the leaf down. The forest floor becomes a blanket of fallen leaves.

scenes.title: A CLOSER LOOK
scenes.caption: Each fallen leaf carries a seasonal record.
scenes.narration: The colors and patterns on a fallen leaf reflect its pigments, its age, and the conditions it experienced during the season.

scenes.title: WIND AND RAIN
scenes.caption: Weather helps move leaves from branches.
scenes.narration: Wind, rain, and cooling temperatures all help finish the process. Different trees release their leaves at different times.

scenes.title: A NATURAL RECYCLING LOOP
scenes.caption: Fallen leaves become part of the soil.
scenes.narration: Fungi, bacteria, and small animals break down fallen leaves. Their nutrients return to the soil and support new growth.

scenes.title: THE FOREST FLOOR
scenes.caption: Decomposition feeds the next season.
scenes.narration: What looks like an ending is also a beginning. Decomposing leaves help build healthy soil for the forest.
